clue.text: Being in nick, aims to be most comfortable

indicators.note: one word being in another means it sits inside it, so the aiming word goes into the nicking word

parts.note: to nick is to cut, as with a razor
shies means throws or aims at, as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: A prisoner in the nick plans to make life as comfy as possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like prison (British slang for jail), but here it is the verb meaning to make a small incision; 'Being in' says the aiming word sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cushy is informal for easy and comfortable, so its superlative means most comfortable.

clue.text: Son in country dance — not the best place for it!

definitions.text: not the best place for it!

indicators.note: the son is placed in the middle of the country-and-dance pair, between the two words

parts.note: China is the country
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A son dancing a country dance, and the venue is unsuitable for such capers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the idiom 'a bull in a china shop': a shop full of crockery is no place for a lively dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A store selling fragile porcelain is proverbially the worst spot for clumsy, boisterous movement.

clue.text: Make hole in fuel container

definitions.meaning: to sink a ship deliberately by holing it
a coal bucket kept by the fireside

explanation.surface: Someone punctures a tank holding fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both deliberately sinking a vessel and the metal coal bucket by a hearth.

clue.text: Trendy men holding function within building

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
a do is a party or social function
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers as opposed to officers

explanation.surface: Fashionable men hosting a party inside some building.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening inside a building, rather than outside, is an indoor event.

clue.text: Real thugs involved in killing

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters are entangled and twisted together into a new order

explanation.surface: Genuine hoodlums took part in a murder.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaughter is mass killing or butchery, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Spotted bishop by reception area

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a lobby is an entrance hall or reception area

explanation.surface: A bishop was seen standing near the reception desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' reads as seen, but it is the adjective meaning covered in spots or blotches.
explanation.definitionFit: Something covered in blobs of colour is blotchy or spotted.

clue.text: Clean and tidy study again?

definitions.meaning: to smarten up by sweeping or grooming
to refresh knowledge of a subject by revising it

explanation.surface: Tidying up and revisiting one's revision.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to groom or sweep tidy and to revise forgotten knowledge.

clue.text: Maidens possibly quiet and unwell — a waste of lager?

parts.note: in cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored, so maidens are an example of overs
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
ill means unwell

explanation.surface: Several maidens, quiet and feeling poorly, perhaps after too much beer.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled; a maiden is one with no runs, which is why 'possibly' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer slopping over the rim of a full glass is wasted liquid that has spilled over.

clue.text: Transport chief providing musical entertainment

parts.note: a bus is a means of transport
a king is a chief or ruler

explanation.surface: The head of a transport company plays music for the public.
explanation.definitionFit: Street performers play music in public places for donations from passers-by.

clue.text: Note of inpecuniousness?

indicators.note: of means taken out of, the letters lying inside the long word that follows

explanation.surface: A written note that reveals a lack of money.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue spells the word with an N; the letters sit in its middle either way.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an informal written acknowledgment of a debt, a promissory slip.

clue.text: Day with student event at Oxford college — folk dressing unconventionally

parts.note: a rag is a British student charity event, often with fancy dress
Queen's is a college of Oxford University

explanation.surface: A day out at a student fundraising event at an Oxford college.
explanation.definitionFit: These are performers, typically men, who dress flamboyantly in women's clothing.

clue.text: Gangster hard outside, hard inside, for all that

parts.note: Al Capone is the stock crossword gangster

indicators.note: the first hard word goes on the outside of the second
the second hard word goes inside the first, so one wraps the other

parts.note: tough means hard
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A gangster tough on the outside but soft-hearted — no, hard within too.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean nevertheless or in spite of that, a conjunction of concession.

clue.text: Strict Jew rejecting part of meal as brought in

indicators.note: the word as is brought into the middle of the turned dish word
rejecting means turning the meal word back, so it reads in the opposite direction

parts.note: a dish is one course or part of a meal

explanation.surface: An observant Jew declines a course of a meal that has been served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' gives HSID, and 'brought in' places the little word after its first letter. This doubled-S form is a variant spelling of Hasid.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hasid is a member of an ultra-orthodox Jewish movement, known for strict observance.

clue.text: In auditorium the man would briefly listen

indicators.note: an auditorium is where an audience listens, so these words signal a sound-alike

parts.note: he would, shortened, becomes he'd

explanation.surface: In a concert hall, a man would listen for a short time.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay attention to advice or a warning is to listen to it.

clue.text: Stopping in India, gent on a detour

indicators.note: taking a detour means going round a different way, so the letters are rerouted

explanation.surface: A gentleman in India halting while on a roundabout route.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding someone back or delaying them is keeping them from going, a synonym of halting.

clue.text: Youths having flings with effect of drug admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the drug's effect is let inside the flings word

parts.note: to fling is to sling or throw
a trip is a hallucinogenic drug experience

explanation.surface: Young people having flirtations, with a drug's effect admitted to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flings' suggests romances, but it is the verb meaning throws.
explanation.definitionFit: A young lad on the verge of manhood is an old-fashioned word for a youth.

clue.text: Bring in worker from abroad? It's vital

parts.note: to import is to bring goods in from overseas
an ant is the crossword worker, from worker ants

explanation.surface: Recruiting labour from overseas is essential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from abroad?' completes the sense of bringing in; the question mark admits the worker is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Something essential or of great significance is vital.

clue.text: Celebrate good-looking female turning up in unmarried state

parts.note: to sing is to celebrate, as in singing someone's praises

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a model is a good-looking woman paid to show clothes

explanation.surface: Celebrate when an attractive woman arrives as a single person.
explanation.definitionFit: Being single, unwed and unattached, is this jocular state.

clue.text: Hang pop art the wrong way in studio frame?

indicators.note: hanging art the wrong way implies the letters are put in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Hanging a pop-art picture upside down in an artist's studio.
explanation.definitionFit: A jointed frame used to copy drawings at scale, or one holding studio lights, fits a frame found in a studio.

clue.text: A beast carrying pot and little bottle

indicators.note: the beast word carries the pot word within it

parts.note: a mule is a beast of burden
a po is a chamber pot

explanation.surface: A pack animal carrying a pot and a small bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small sealed glass vial, typically holding a dose of medicine.

clue.text: Stagger around as someone who tries to be funny

definitions.text: someone who tries to be funny

indicators.note: around means the letters are moved about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Lurching about like a would-be comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: A joker who tells jokes and wisecracks, trying for laughs.

clue.text: See leg revealed by bird

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: A leg is seen, exposed by a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The leg side of a cricket field is the half behind the batter's legs, also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: A diving water bird known in Britain as the diver.

clue.text: Ham it up as singing dame in the course of month

indicators.note: in the course of means during, so the dame sits within the month

parts.note: Oct is the abbreviation for October
Dame Vera Lynn was the British wartime singer

explanation.surface: A singing dame camps it up during some month.
explanation.definitionFit: To exaggerate a performance theatrically is to perform too hammily.

clue.text: Get more by redeveloping an early version?

indicators.note: redeveloping means rebuilding, so the letters are reconstructed

explanation.surface: Making more money by rebuilding an earlier design.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in its first rudimentary stage, before full development, is in its germinal form.

clue.text: It's bound to be a time of growth

definitions.meaning: a leap or jump, the noun sense
the season when plants start to grow

explanation.surface: Something that must surely be a season of growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's bound to be' reads as certainty, but 'bound' is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both a jump and the season between winter and summer.

clue.text: Bringer of order against his king we will see here

definitions.text: Bringer of order against his king we will see here

parts.note: CR is Carolus Rex, King Charles, the monarch the Lord Protector fought
OM is the Order of Merit
we will contracts to we'll

explanation.surface: The man who imposed order against his own king is found right here.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the Parliamentarian leader who defeated Charles I; 'see here' points to the pieces making him.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver of Huntingdon led the Parliamentary side against Charles I and ruled as Lord Protector.

clue.text: Awaiting a decision — from ground control?

definitions.meaning: aircraft aloft, as viewed by air traffic controllers on the ground

explanation.surface: A decision pending, as relayed by the control tower.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means unsettled, and literally describes planes aloft awaiting landing clearance.

clue.text: Tot knocks the edges of father

indicators.note: knocking off the edges means the first and last letters of the father word go

parts.note: daddy is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A toddler bumps into the corners of their dad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a small child, but it is the verb, as in tot up.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot up figures is to sum them.

clue.text: Tramp in pub eating food

indicators.note: the pub word eats the food, taking it inside

parts.note: a bar is a pub
an egg is a food

explanation.surface: A vagrant in a pub having something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagrant who lives by asking for money is a tramp.

clue.text: Where this answer goes, in reality

definitions.meaning: the entry sits on the lowest row of the grid

explanation.surface: Wondering where this entry fits, in truth.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means basically or fundamentally, and literally names the grid's last row.
